ports.note: Every layer port, on every map, whatever its parameters say. The ports used to vary with an inputMode parameter -- reasoningInput, rasterInput, polygonInput, networkInput were four separate declarations of that -- so the port a connection needed might not exist on the node. Which renderer draws is now read from what is wired: src/core.ts#drawnMode.

ontology.note: Map presentation plan and MapView activity are implemented; broader map artifact and cartographic contracts remain open. 0.11.0 declared fw:MapSpecification and the fifteen encoding properties here. That was wrong: emits records what the module named in implementation.definition asserts, and this widget is defined in src/core.ts#TYPES, which asserts nothing. The encoding terms are asserted by src/map-communication.ts and are gated by validate:ontology-coupling, which holds at zero undeclared. A release file is immutable, so 0.11.0 keeps the over-declaration and this one corrects it.

changes.description: Value classes count each unit once, not each of its parts. A district drawn in 83 parts, Bonthe in Sierra Leone, filled half the values the quantiles were cut from, so two breaks fell on its rate and the key printed an empty class, "6.72 to 6.72". Every part is still drawn and coloured by its unit's class.

evidence.note: Repository regression coverage exists; this release entry does not certify a widget independently. The self-description added in 0.17.0 is covered by tests/artifact-notes.test.mjs (13 unit checks, including that nothing machined numbers its own artifact or calls itself a caption, that an unnamed artifact is left unnamed rather than titled, and that a unit is stated once) and by tests/equation-notes.browser.mjs over the South London example on Chromium and WebKit. Both were mutation-checked by reintroducing the behaviour they forbid. 0.21.1: tests/value-classes.test.mjs checks that 98 parts of 16 units give the 16 units' breaks, with no equal breaks and no empty class, and that two units sharing a name still count twice.
